What did you notice? Capture the details worth remembering.
Write down what you notice. Your notes stay on this device, even when you’re offline.
Try a different search or choose another project.
This note cannot be changed safely. Its saved contents have been kept. Update the app or contact support before changing it.
The server did not accept this note. You can edit it below, or retry after correcting the server problem. Your local version is preserved.
The server did not accept this deletion. The note stays here for review. Retry after correcting the server problem to synchronize the deletion.
This note could not be loaded. Try again to check its current state.
The editor could not load the note and projects. Your draft is preserved. Retry to continue editing.
This draft can no longer safely replace the original note. Your text is preserved below. Save it as a new note, or load the latest version to start again.
Loading the latest version replaces your unsaved draft. To keep this text, cancel and save it as a new note first. If the original is no longer available, your draft will be kept.
This note is no longer available.
The server changed while this device had unsynced edits. Keep this device’s version to retry it against the latest server revision, or replace it with the server version.
Capture what you noticed, then save it to your journal. You can write offline.
Use a title of 120 characters or fewer.
Something went wrong. Your saved notes are safe. Please try again.
This sync pass finished. Background sync will continue the remaining changes.
Some changes have an uncertain server response. They are preserved for a safe background retry.
Your changes are preserved, but background retry could not be started. Try Sync now again.
Sync took too long. Your changes are preserved. Try Sync now again.
Sync took too long. Your changes are preserved and background retry is queued.
Background sync is paused. Use Sync now to try again.
Sync finished. Review the notes marked as conflicts.
Check your server access token in Settings to synchronize.
Allow local network access in Settings to synchronize with your local server. Your notes are saved on this device.
Could not connect. Changes are saved locally and queued to retry.
Sync could not use the server response. Your changes are preserved. Check the server and try Sync now again.
Some changes need your attention. Open the notes marked as paused to review or retry them.
Show more notes in less space.

Your choice overrides the assignment. Activity with an override is excluded from experiment comparisons.
Record usage counts and error types on this device only. Note text, project names, and credentials are never included.
Get a quiet confirmation after your changes sync successfully. Android may ask for permission when you turn this on.
Notification permission was not granted. Notes and sync still work.
Sync stays on this device. No server or access token is needed.
Notes and demo sync data stay in this app. Uninstalling clears them.
Your access token is saved securely. Sync will check whether the server accepts it.
Add your local server’s access token to sync. You can keep writing offline.
Use the server’s FIELDNOTES_TOKEN value: 24–4096 printable ASCII characters. The token is encrypted on this device.
Android 17 requires permission to connect to your local development server. Allow local network access when you want to synchronize with that server. Offline notes remain available without it.
Local network access is allowed. Your local server must also be running to synchronize.
Local network access has not been allowed.
Local network access was not granted. You can keep writing offline, try again, or allow access in Android app settings.
Notes are stored in the app’s private database. Removing a credential does not erase notes. This single-workspace sample has no multi-account switching. Uninstalling clears local app data.
Trace one observation from the screen to storage, through a sync, and back again.
Compose renders immutable state from a ViewModel. Actions travel down through use cases and repository interfaces. Room observations travel up as Flow. The domain module has no Android dependency.
Save with airplane mode on. Close and reopen the app. Your note remains because the local database is the source of truth. WorkManager retries durable background work when its constraints allow.
A server revision detects conflicting edits. Local changes remain available until a response is acknowledged safely. Try editing the same note on two devices, then choose which version to keep.

Routine tests call domain and ViewModel methods with fakes and controlled coroutine dispatchers. HTTP and preference tests check method boundaries on the JVM. Device and server integrations are optional manual checks. Screens are reviewed visually; there are no functional UI tests.
Rotate the editor to check draft restoration. Background and reopen the app to see lifecycle-aware collection. Open the legacy screen to inspect a Java Fragment and XML View alongside Compose.

The repository includes delivery checks, a performance measurement plan, and a release runbook. Real identity, cloud monitoring, Play publication, accessibility audits, and production usage require external setup and evidence.
Read README, DESIGN, and the requirements map in the source project for the guided exercises and exact verification status.
